column3: The Hebrew says this is the house and this is the altar; BSB makes both statements prospective with here shall be.
The Hebrew commands gathering the resident foreigners and appoints stonecutters without an explicit from whom; BSB supplies that link.
The Hebrew calls Solomon young and tender; BSB uses young and inexperienced.
The Hebrew leaves the one calling Solomon unnamed; BSB names David.
The Hebrew says in his days; BSB specifies during his reign.
The Hebrew separately says succeed and build; BSB combines these as succeeding in building.
The Hebrew describes the preparation as in my affliction; BSB renders this taking great pains.
The Hebrew says there is no number after listing the materials, without repeating a noun for craftsmen; BSB supplies craftsmen beyond number.
The Hebrew calls the future building the house; BSB calls it the temple.
